question: Does each of 13 of the workstation's 16 catalog-evidence tools (PR #296) run inside an Ultracode workflow subagent on this WSL2 authoring laptop, reusing that reference's own tasks for those 13 unchanged, and do the tools' own counters, an exact tokenizer, and a second, independent verifier subagent agree?
method: The 13 tools and their tasks are reused unchanged from the workstation's own catalog evidence (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json, PR #296), recorded verbatim on this host as reference-tasks.json. Each subagent's own computed task is a host adaptation of that same reference task where the reference's exact target does not exist on this host or this host's own instructions name a different one; every such change is recorded per tool under deviations_from_reference. Only 13 of the reference's 16 tools were run: codebase-memory-mcp, agentsview and otel-tui are not among the 13 (see retained_failures_and_gaps for why each was left out).

One Sonnet 5 workflow subagent per tool (label e2e:<tool>) did real work against a disposable detached worktree R = nas-e2e-R at commit 9a8257cd (origin/main), or the session project root (agent-lab) where a tool is bound to it. It wrote the baseline only by shell redirect or an equivalent read-only extraction, read only the tool's own output, answered from that output, and ran one deterministic PASS/FAIL check of the answer against the baseline.

A second, independent Opus 5.5 workflow subagent per tool (label verify:<tool>) reproduced the check from the same, unchanged pair files, re-ran the tool's own channel where feasible, checked the channel and binary provenance against upstream, and returned a verdict (confirmed or refuted) plus supporting notes; recorded per tool under verifier.

Upstream lifetime counters (rtk gain --format json, once project-scoped and once global; headroom savings --json; jCodeMunch get_session_stats/persistent ledger; Context Mode stats files) were captured immediately before (2026-09-26T00:35:58Z) and after (2026-09-26T01:13:57Z) the workflow run.

Each baseline/tool-output pair was compared exactly with the pinned o200k_base tokenizer (gpt-tokenizer) and recorded in a private host-side ledger (token-evidence/ledger.sqlite3); each exact_comparison.recorded_at below is that comparison's own ledger timestamp.
Provider consumption of every child comes from child-usage.mjs over this workflow's own transcript (wf_0893832e-937).

Three role-scoped probe subagents (source-scout, evidence-reviewer, isolated-builder) each tried the same set of lanes (RTK, QMD, Serena, SocratiCode, jCodeMunch, Context Mode, ai-memory, and for one role a ToolSearch/deferred-schema lane) to record which lanes each role's own tool allowlist can reach; recorded under role_access_probes.

evidence_classes.subagent_tool_use: native_proven on this host for all 13 tools (each marked worked_in_subagent: true): the tool ran for real inside the e2e subagent and its answer was checked against a baseline; a second, independent verify subagent reproduced the check and returned its own verdict.
evidence_classes.exact_comparisons: local_integration: exact o200k_base artifact token counts for one task each, from this host's pinned tokenizer via the private ledger; they are not provider-billed savings and must not be summed with upstream estimates or with each other.
evidence_classes.baseline_kind: counterfactual_raw pairs (baseline.txt is the actual raw content -- a real file, or the same commands' unfiltered output -- that the tool made unnecessary to read in full) may be read as a reduction when tokens_removed is positive. check_ground_truth pairs (baseline.txt is a minimal derived fixture -- a grep/SQL/API excerpt built only to verify the tool's answer, never the real counterfactual) are never a reduction claim, regardless of the sign of tokens_removed. 5 of 13 tools here are check_ground_truth (context-mode, repomix, serena, socraticode, ai-memory) and all 5 show a negative tokens_removed, exactly as expected for that category; 3 more counterfactual_raw tools (headroom, qmd, toon) also show a negative number because their captured tool-output artifact bundles more than the efficient representation alone (headroom's tool-output.txt holds the compress AND retrieve AND stats responses together; qmd's holds the preceding search listing plus qmd's own per-line numbering overhead on top of the retrieved document; toon's holds both the encoded TOON body and the decoded-back JSON from the round-trip check) -- see the README for the full worked classification.
evidence_classes.upstream_counters: upstream_estimate: each tool's own accounting. rtk's project-scoped and global gain, headroom's lifetime ledger, jCodeMunch's persistent ledger and Context Mode's stats files are host-wide over the window (or, for Context Mode, drawn from two different sessions entirely) and include other concurrent activity, so their deltas are not cleanly attributable to this run alone. Of these, only jCodeMunch's persistent-ledger delta isolates to this run's own commands, and even that is labelled an estimate (its own savings_provenance basis is a benchmark citation, not a per-call measurement -- see the jcodemunch tool entry's verifier notes). rtk's project-scoped gain does NOT isolate: it is still host-wide across every session bound to this project (see counters.rtk_gain_project_scoped below), not a per-run figure.
evidence_classes.verifier_review: second_pass: an independent Opus 5.5 subagent (verify:<tool>) reproduced each check from the unchanged pair files, re-ran the tool's own channel where feasible, and checked upstream provenance; its verdict (confirmed/refuted) and notes are recorded per tool. 'confirmed' means the e2e subagent's report is accurate about what it found -- not that the tool itself passed cleanly; rtk (refuted on two specific factual claims despite a passing check) and, within their own narrower checks, serena and repomix (both confirmed as accurate reports of a check that itself failed or partially failed) illustrate the difference.

My stricter check scores 19/21, with both failures on CMD2, on the original pair and on the fresh recapture (verify/independent-check.txt, verify/independent-check-recapture.txt).

The producer never tested the -C form of this exclusion.

The shortened path '/.../sota-convergence/README.md' matches 2 different raw files (verify/check-recall.txt).

What does hold: the hook rewrites plain git/ls/grep; git log, find and diff pass through; the excluded git log output is byte-identical; the measured savings are real; and fidelity holds for CMD1 and CMD3-6.
